FOUR of the six named clusters CLOSED. (1) Six rebase `add` words, target base-first versus ours offset-first - the largest single win at 92 -> 80, and it was hiding under a RENAMING label; see claim.law.rebase-add-operand-order-follows-source-expression.20260831.v1. (2) The node-info loop counter, moved to the target's early position by the counter-first while form. (3) The per-match loop's counter/stride update ORDER plus its preheader init order, 80 -> 78. (4) The tail: the target's latched-slot guard is an EARLY RETURN, not an if/else assigning slot - proven by its branch going to +0x8e8, past the return-register setup, while `clrlwi r3,r3,17` writes the result straight into r3. That single restructure closed both the branch-target skew at +0x160 and the `addi r3,r30,0` versus `mr r3,r30` word, 78 -> 72. (5) Two of the four reloc rows closed by claiming .sbss 0x803441E8 as natreelists. REMAINING, 3 STRUCTURAL / 6 unpaired, both mechanisms fully named and both DO-NOT-RETRY. (a) TWO reloc rows at +0x24/+0x28: a .bss ARRAY reloc where MWCC names the section and the dtk split names a manufactured symbol - a split artifact, not source-reachable; the `static`-removal hypothesis was tested and falsified at a cost of 13 real and instruction parity. (b) TWO zero-constant clusters, `li` + copy in the texmod and per-match preheaders where the target rematerialises both zeros, plus the 4-byte pairing skew they induce. Three distinct carrier identities probed, all negative and all with the same conserved signature; the sibling-loop law proves the choice is allocator-side. The zero-copy class is the function's remaining WebFrank candidate but needs the dataflow-equivalence audit, not copy_register_fields.
